messages:
mike: Observed priming-buffer miss-rate spike after last night's canary (async-kernel-v2 + quant-attn q2). Quick dump below.

mike: metrics:
```
window: 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z - 2026-03-17T05:00:00Z
serving: model-x-v3 (quant q2), kernel: async-v2
priming_hit: 0.63 (was 0.94 baseline)
p50_latency: 42ms -> 68ms
error_rate: +0.3%
sampled_requests: 12k
```

mike: quick note: this is on dedicated pool eu-west-1a, traffic routed by policy=latency-prefer

sophia: can you paste a few cache keys (hashed and unhashed) from failed vs hit requests? suspect canonicalization/tokenization normalization changed w/ compiler tweak

mike: pasted examples:
```
hit_key: "ctx_v1::user:774::toknorm:0::sha1:7a8f..."
miss_key: "ctx_v1::user:774::toknorm:1::sha1:9b2c..."
miss_key2: "ctx_v1::user:774::toknorm:0::sha1:7a8f...::pad=1"
```

raj: interesting — I see extra ::pad suffix on miss_key2. any code that appends padding bit after async kernel reorder? also check kvcache seed/version (we bumped seed in the compiler PR)

taylor: I ran a trace on canary node. kernel async-v2 reorders attention tiling which changed how prefix tokens are marshalled into the KV proto. I see the canonicalizer in runtime now emits `::pad=1` for sequences that used to be suppressed. attaching brief trace:
```
trace snippets:
marshal_prefix -> canonicalize_keys (old): strip_pad=false -> key=\"ctx_v1::user...::toknorm:0\"
marshal_prefix -> canonicalize_keys (async-v2): strip_pad=true? -> produced key with \"::pad=1\"
```

taylor: looks like a bool flip in canonicalize callsite. also compiler changed quant profile to q2 which moved token offsets when using fused-attn -> different tokenization alignment

sophia: also check batching heuristics; async kernel changed batch boundary guarantees so prefix reuse across requests might be less frequent during small B=1 bursts

mike: observed hit rate drop correlates with both pad-suffix and small-burst window (burstiness metric up). we should confirm whether canonicalize change was intentional. pinging @deploy-bot for rollout details

deploy-bot: canary rollout async-kernel-v2 started 2026-03-17T01:45Z; at 01:50Z switched quant profile to q2 on canary nodes; canary target=10% traffic; change authored by @ing-compilers (PR 1124) — link: https://git.internal/pr/1124

raj: plan: 1) revert canonicalize change on canary to previous strip behavior, 2) add compatibility shim to ignore pad suffix in key normalization, 3) add an eval harness to fuzz key variants and compute hit delta. can someone own revert + shim?

mike: I'll take revert on canary now. starting hotfix branch. will report back with hit-rate in 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

taylor: I'll add a short unit test for marshal/canonicalize to prevent future flips.

sophia: Also file an Optimize suggestion to evaluate quant profile q2 aliasing effects on token alignment. might be separate but worth tracking.

mike: thanks team. temporary mitigation: canary revert applied, priming_hit back to 0.91 after ~20min. logging evidence below:
```
after revert window:
priming_hit: 0.91
p50_latency: 44ms
```

mike: creating follow-up issue with traces + sample keys. leaving thread open for follow-ups.
